'''Amir Yacoby''' (born around 1964) is a condensed matter physicist and professor at [[Harvard University]].

His work is focused on investigation techniques for quantum matter, such as [[quantum sensing]] with [[Quantum dot|quantum dots]] and [[color centers]] (see [[Nitrogen-vacancy center]]), and on [[quantum computing]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amir Yacoby – NAS |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/amir-yacoby-veensl/ |access-date=2026-10-01 |website=nasonline |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Education==
Yacoby got bachelor’s degree in aeronautical engineering and a master’s degree in theoretical physics.<ref name = ":1">{{cite web |url=https://www.physics.harvard.edu/people/facpages/yacoby |title=Amir Yacoby |website=physics.harvard.edu |access-date=2024-12-19}}</ref> In 1994, he obtained his PhD at [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] under the supervision of Professor [[Moty Heiblum]].

==Career==
In 2006, Yacoby started teaching at Harvard.<ref name = ":1" /> He was appointed as the Lazaridis Chair in Physics of the [[Institute for Quantum Computing]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/institute-for-quantum-computing/news/institute-quantum-computing-adds-former-csa-chief-harvard|title=Institute for Quantum Computing adds former CSA chief, Harvard professor|publisher=University of Waterloo|date=September 9, 2013|accessdate=December 6, 2019}}</ref> In March 2014, his group developed a [[magnetic resonance imaging]] technology by which nanoscale images can be provided, that could enable researchers to peer into the atomic structure of individual molecules.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://phys.org/news/2014-04-mri-molecular-scale-team-peer.html|title=MRI, on a molecular scale: Team develops system that could peer into atomic structure of individual molecules|date=April 18, 2014|website=[[Phys.org]]|accessdate=December 6, 2019}}</ref> In 2014, Yacoby was named a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/new-aaas-fellows-recognized-their-contributions-advancing-science|author=Kat Zambon|title=New AAAS Fellows Recognized for Their Contributions to Advancing Science|publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science|date=November 24, 2014|accessdate=December 6, 2019}}</ref>

Amir Yacoby is co-founder of the start-up Quantum Elements, which was founded in 2023 in Los Angeles.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-22 |title=Quantum Elements Launches AI-native Platform for Quantum Software and Hardware Development |url=https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/quantum-elements-launches-ai-native-platform-for-quantum-software-and-hardware-development/ |access-date=2026-10-02 |website=HPCwire |language=en-US}}</ref> It is offering a "quantum development software stack" for simulation of quantum computing hardware.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Platform Features |url=https://quantumelements.ai/features |access-date=2026-10-02 |website=Quantum Elements |language=en}}</ref>

In September 2026, it was announced that Yacoby would be appointed as inaugural "Ray Dolby Professor of Theoretical and Experimental Physics" at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2026-09-25 |title=Professor Amir Yacoby appointed inaugural Ray Dolby Professor of Theoretical and Experimental Physics |url=https://www.phy.cam.ac.uk/news/professor-amir-yacoby-appointed-inaugural-ray-dolby-professor-of-theoretical-and-experimental-physics/ |access-date=2026-10-01 |website=Cavendish Laboratory Department of Physics |language=EN}}</ref>
